newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, October 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Thursday, October 3.

text.p: Following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.
*The Democratic party of the Left will seek to abolish the new housing tax included in the 1997 budget (all).
* German Chancellor Helmut Kohl in Dublin says criteria for joining Emu will be discussed in 1998. "So, why don't we wait and see?" (all).

* Foreign minister Lamberto Dini in an interview says: "I know the Maastricht criteria will not be softened. I believe there will be a general assessment to decide whether it would be worthwhile to delay a bit the start (of the single currency), taking into account also 1998 and not only 1997" (La Repubblica).
* New record high for Italian Btp futures, climbing to 123,40 as the lira hits a two-year high against the mark (all).
* Trade Unions say the Italian state Post service is seeking to cut 20.000 jobs (La Stampa, Corriere).

* The 1997 budget include a 1.500 billion lire provision for state industrial holding group Iri to cover losses of troubled flag carrier Alitalia. Alitalia posted a 310 billion lire loss in the first half of 1996 (Il Sole 24 Ore).

* Olivetti might sell an eight per cent stake in Omnitel to German group Mannesmann, which already holds a stake in the mobile telephone consortium. New chief executive Roberto Colaninno is scheduled to meet analysts today in Milan (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
